text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government going ahead with building of third terminal costing Singapore $1.5 billion at Changi Airport.
- Parliamentary debate on committee report recommending fines against opposition leaders postponed to December 11 due to absence of members of their party.

- Finance Minister Richard Hu seeks parliamentary approval for government spending amounting to S$11.4 billion to ensure goverment has enough resources to keep running up to August next year if parliament adjourned on January 5, 1997.
- U.S. and Japan sign agreement to reduce size of American military bases on Okinawa and announce plans for floating heliport off the island.
- Utility group Singapore Power and Singapore Technologies Telemedia will jointly bid for Singapore's second nationwide, full-service telephone licence.
- First collective sale by auction to be held next month when 32-unit apartment building in Scotts Road goes on block.
- Four remisiers charged with criminal breach of trust in recent months.
- Taiwan's ruling Kuomintang party transferring assets of around US$30 million from Hong Kong to Singapore.
- Outlook for Asian equities in next couple of years very promising, with several major money managers turning bullish on emerging Asia.
- New issue Wee Poh Holdings finishes maiden trading day with 84 percent gain.
- Creative Technology shares soar as much as 31 percent following gains in New York.
- Scotts Holdings seeks shareholder approval to diversify into property development.
- Mainboard listed Parkway Holdings announces plans to restructure healthcare business in Indonesia.
